incontrovertible

in-kon-truh-VUR-ti-bul · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Incontrovertible is not able to be denied or disputed.

The security footage provided incontrovertible proof that the suspect had never left his apartment that night.

Example

The lab's results were incontrovertible: three independent tests all confirmed the exact same measurement to the decimal point.

Incontrovertible is reserved for evidence or facts so solid that no reasonable person could argue against them.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

undeniable: Undeniable means so plainly true that even someone who wishes otherwise must admit it -- undeniable talent, undeniable charm. It often describes qualities people concede at a glance. Incontrovertible is its courtroom-strength cousin: reserved for facts and proof so complete that the dispute itself is over.

irrefutable: Irrefutable means impossible to prove wrong: every attempt to knock the claim down fails. Incontrovertible makes a matching claim about facts and proof, with a different emphasis -- irrefutable says all attacks fail, while incontrovertible says no real dispute can even be raised.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

debatable: open to argument

dubious: doubtful or questionable

Where it sits · how little room for doubt remains

convincing → incontrovertible → self-evident

convincing vs. incontrovertible: Convincing sits well below incontrovertible: a convincing argument wins most people over but might still have a weak point, while incontrovertible proof shuts the question completely.

self-evident vs. incontrovertible: Self-evident goes a step beyond incontrovertible: incontrovertible proof defeats every dispute with evidence, while a self-evident truth -- two plus two is four -- needs no evidence at all, because doubt never even gets started.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — in-: not (Latin)

root+suffix — controvertible: able to be disputed (Latin (controvertere))

Put it together: in- ("not") + controvertible ("able to be disputed") = not able to be denied or argued against.

Use the root in a new word: controversy: The new mascot stirred up a controversy that lasted well into spring.
